html:
The Apurinã, who call themselves Popũkare, are an Amazonian people of the Purus River basin in western Brazil. They speak an Arawakan language.

They live in villages along the Purus and its tributaries, growing manioc and hunting and fishing. Early visitors described their long, low houses with walls and roof made as one, their small bark canoes and their poisoned arrows. The rubber boom of the late 1800s brought thousands of rubber tappers up the Purus, who took their land and forced many into labour. Today several thousand Apurinã live in the states of Amazonas, Acre and Rondônia in Brazil, among the forest farmers of the western Amazon.
